summary: An announcement that a US Air Force weather center would provide years of surface and upper-air weather observations through the datacomputer. A working group was formed to design the database, plan tests and tackle technical issues, and interested users were invited to join.

eli5.summary: A big collection of weather records will be put on the network for anyone to use, and a team is organizing how.

subtitle: A major weather database served through the ARPA Network

tldr.problem: Researchers need access to large amounts of historical weather observations.
tldr.mechanism: The US Air Force Environmental Technical Applications Center (ETAC) provides ten years of surface and upper-air weather data through the datacomputer, a specialized network node designed for shared databases.
tldr.outcome: The data becomes available to network researchers through a working group coordinating the database design, implementation and testing.

today: This was an early announcement of shared network data services. The ETAC weather dataset represented one of the first major shared scientific databases accessible through the ARPA Network.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: RFC 251 announces the availability of weather data from the US Air Force Environmental Technical Applications Center (ETAC) for the ARPA Network. The dataset ultimately will contain ten years of high-quality surface and upper-air weather observations, generated by approximately 5,000 surface and 1,200 upper-air weather stations distributed worldwide, plus hemispheric grid point analyses.
sections.eli5: The Air Force is sharing years of weather measurements from thousands of stations around the world on the computer network.

sections.title: The Datacomputer Node
sections.content: The data is made available through the datacomputer, a specialized node of the ARPA Network dedicated to managing shared databases and designed to accommodate large ones. The datacomputer, then under development by Computer Corporation of America (CCA), will provide services for accessing these databases, including the weather data.
sections.eli5: A special computer on the network is built just to store and hand out big databases like this one.

sections.title: The Working Group
sections.content: A working group has been formed to design the database structure, coordinate its implementation with datacomputer development, plan testing, project potential uses, and resolve technical issues associated with the database's size and complexity. Prospective users and interested parties are encouraged to participate.
sections.eli5: A team is planning how to organize the data, test it and help people use it.

sections.title: Getting Involved
sections.content: Prospective users, working group members, or interested parties should contact Dale H. Stern at Computer Corporation of America, 575 Technology Square, Cambridge, Massachusetts 02139, or call (617) 491-3670. The RFC refers to RFC 219 for more details about the datacomputer's service model.
sections.eli5: If you want to use the weather data or help design it, call or write Dale Stern in Cambridge.

references.text: McKenzie, A., "User Interface to ARPANET Datacomputer", RFC 219.
